sourceOfTruth: packages/vue-vscode live tree joined to the DX0 product-receipt-basis hostIdentity field, the VSC0 host-separation contract and the BWH0 platform-host-services law
law: Browser-local and remote-native are distinct products with distinct receipts. The active host/backend is visible and correct in every browser-connected workspace (VSW0-AC2): a remote Node service serving a browser client is not browser-local parity.

browser-local.definition: Extension code executes in the browser web extension host (web worker) on the user's machine: vscode.dev / github.dev local web workers. Semantic work rides the BWH wasm host through in-memory platform services; the browser closure has no process, filesystem, socket or thread capability.
browser-local.derivesFrom: executing entry = browser entry; workspace topology = local web workspace

remote-native.definition: Extension code executes in a remote Node extension host (Codespaces, SSH, WSL, tunnel/reverse-proxy). A browser is only the viewport: viewing or editing through vscode.dev does not make this browser-local, and it may never claim browser-local receipts.
remote-native.derivesFrom: workspace topology = remote extension host; client kind is irrelevant

desktop-local.definition: Extension code executes in the local desktop Node extension host (VS Code desktop). The Node transport, binary discovery and child spawn are desktop-owned (VSC0 transport-desktop-owned).
desktop-local.derivesFrom: executing entry = main entry; workspace topology = local

companion-native.definition: Explicitly selected authenticated local native companion execution (DX4/DX5 route; VSW4N owns the opt-in selector). A browser-local product with one labelled native execution rail: companion results carry the companion engine identity and version and never merge silently into browser-local results.
companion-native.derivesFrom: browser-local execution plus an explicit user-selected companion connection

claims: browser-local parity for a feature exists only when its WebExtensionFeatureContract webDisposition route is live; a protocol smoke or screenshot is not real-editor responsiveness or semantic-correctness proof
a remote Node service serving a browser client is not browser-local parity; it is remote-native and displays as remote-native
unsupported in browser-local mode is the DX0 unsupported completeness state, surfaced on the feature surface — never dropped diagnostics, weakened typing or a silently removed feature
companion-native execution is explicitly selected, authenticated and labelled; guessing a companion connection or hiding its identity is a failing claim
the desktop extension and the web entry are one product family over one producer set (VSC0 browser-is-distinct-product); neither may claim the other's receipts

visibility.rule: The active host status is derived from the executing entry and the workspace topology, never guessed from the client kind, and it is surfaced: bound to the hostIdentity receipt field on every feature result and displayed on the provider status surface. A wrong or hidden host status is a failing claim, not a degraded mode.

binding.hostIdentity: the executing host per this vocabulary (browser runtime plus WASM build selector, remote extension host, desktop extension host, or the selected companion), carried on the DX0 product-receipt-basis hostIdentity field
binding.surface: the provider-status surface the desktop extension already renders (statusBar binding) gains the web status; every feature result carries the same binding
